title: Petronas Towers
blurb: Cesar Pelli’s 1998 twin supertalls in Kuala Lumpur: 88 floors and 451.9 m on eight-pointed star plans, joined at levels 41 and 42 by a double-decker skybridge, the world’s tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004 and still the tallest twins.

sourceUrls.label: Engineering.com: Petronas Twin Towers at a glance
Sceen-it: Entrapment at the Petronas Towers

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: The 4.5 m concrete rafts on 104 barrette piles 60 to 115 m deep, among the deepest foundations in the world. Pile counts shown schematically.

systems.name: Podium and concourse
systems.description: The podium blocks, lobbies, retail concourse, mosque and roof garden at the towers’ feet. Layout is schematic.

systems.name: Tower shafts
systems.description: The eight setback shaft sections of each tower on the eight-pointed star plan, two interlocking squares standing for unity, harmony, stability and rationality.

systems.name: Setback terraces
systems.description: The terraces at each setback level. Exact setback positions are schematic.

systems.name: Crowns and spires
systems.description: The spire bases, the stainless steel spires completing the 451.9 m height, and the corner pinnacles. Profiles are schematic.

systems.name: Skybridge
systems.description: The double-decker skybridge at levels 41 and 42, 58.4 m long and 170 m up, moving independently of the towers in wind and doubling as a fire escape.

systems.name: Facade
systems.description: Stainless steel cladding (65,000 sq m), glass curtain wall (77,000 sq m), Islamic pattern screens and mullions. Band divisions are schematic.

systems.name: Vertical transport
systems.description: The stiff central lift cores of the tube-in-tube structure, double-deck lift cars, escalators and sky lobbies. Positions are schematic.

systems.name: Crown amenities and park
systems.description: The level 86 observation deck at 370 m, mechanical floors, the KLCC park and fountains, and aircraft warning lights.

explanations.skybridge deck: The double-decker skybridge joining the towers at levels 41 and 42: 58.4 m long, 170 m above street level, weighing 750 tons. It is not rigidly fixed to either tower, so it can move independently in wind, and it serves as a fire escape.
